question: Will the Kennedy Center's main building be open to the general public on October 2, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo flipped on 2026-09-16: building physically fenced and closed, and the actor controlling the decision (board chaired by Trump, executive director reporting to it) has repeatedly and publicly stated it wants a multi-year closure, with Trump conditioning reopening on his name going on the building. The stated 7-day duration expires ~Sept 23 but is explicitly 'subject to weekly reevaluation,' and a partial ceiling collapse plus roof-canopy inspection supply unlimited runway for extension. Cooper's PI has an express carve-out for congressionally authorized repair work, and he DENIED Beatty's emergency hearing on Sept 17 — so the judicial check is real but slow and currently not forcing reopening. The NSO has already relocated its full 2026-27 season, removing the operational imperative to reopen. YES requires either a court order after the Sept 23 status report plus physical compliance inside ~week, or a token reopening to protect the 'temporary' framing on appeal — both plausible, neither favored. Base rate for a major venue reopening within ~16 days of an abrupt structural-safety closure is ~35%; adjusted down hard for the controlling actor's revealed preference for permanent closure, the fencing, and the emptied calendar; adjusted up slightly for litigation-posture incentives and Cooper's demonstrated willingness to rule against the administration.
calls.reference_class: Major public venues/landmark buildings abruptly closed for structural-safety reasons after a partial ceiling/structural failure, where the controlling authority has an independent stated intent to keep the building closed — fraction reopening to general public within ~2.5 weeks
